extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing entry, denial, and processing of applicant amendments after allowance, including amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 and manner-of-amending rules under 37 CFR 1.121. Targets examiners and practitioners handling post-allowance amendments, drawings, and reissue/amendment formality issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely processing of expedited replies (37 CFR 1.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicants use the expedited procedure under 37 CFR 1.116 and properly mark the envelope/papers, the SPE will ensure prompt action and the Office goal is to mail the examiner's action on the reply within 1 month from receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must mark envelope/papers correctly to obtain benefit; delays caused by applicant actions (delayed interviews, further replies, petitions) may prevent achieving the goal. If no action is received within the goal plus normal mailing time, contact the SPE or Group Director. Technical support staff designated to expedite processing will type and mail the action promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Ex parte Quayle (amendments after allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: After all claims have been allowed (Ex parte Quayle), prosecution on the merits is closed even if formal objections remain; amendments touching the merits are treated similarly to amendments after final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.51 for Quayle actions. A shortened statutory two-month period for reply is set in Quayle actions. Prosecution may continue only for formal matters; adding claims or reopening merits is a matter of grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments received around mailing of Notice of Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment that reaches the Office after the notice of allowance has been mailed has the status of an amendment filed under 37 CFR 1.312 and its entry is a matter of grace. If the amendment was filed in the Office before mailing but received by the examiner after mailing, it is treated as though the notice had not been mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application has not been closed to further prosecution (e.g., not all claims allowed/finally rejected), applicant may be entitled to have the amendment entered and withdrawal from issue may be unnecessary if the examiner would recommend entry under 1.312.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 — general rule for post-allowance amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may be made as a matter of right after mailing of the Notice of Allowance. Amendments filed before payment of the issue fee may be entered on the recommendation of the primary examiner and approval by the Commissioner; amendments filed after payment of the issue fee require a petition with fee and a showing of good and sufficient reasons under 37 CFR 1.312(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of amendments falling under 1.312 include changes to the specification, drawings, claims, inventorship, and submission of prior art. The Commissioner has delegated approval of 1.312(a) recommendations to supervisory patent examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental oath/declaration treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in reissue applications, a supplemental oath or declaration is not treated as an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312; however, a supplemental reissue oath/declaration is treated as an amendment under 1.312 because it effects a correction of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue oaths submitted after allowance, the reissue applicant must comply with 37 CFR 1.312 as set forth in the Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner authority on formal corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Notice of Allowance, the primary examiner may make examiner's amendments and may enter amendments that merely correct formal matters in spec/drawings or formal matters in a claim without changing scope, or cancel claims, without forwarding to the supervisory patent examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments other than mere formal corrections require SPE approval. The examiner should indicate 'Enter Formal Matters Only' for such entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group policy for trivial informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Group Director establishes policy for treatment of amendments directed to trivial informalities, with focus on (A) disclosure being adequately clear and (B) invention defined with sufficient clarity to form basis for an enforceable contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy addresses whether trivial informal changes that seldom affect vital formal requirements may be entered without substantial Office work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for considering entry under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 1.312 may be entered when shown (A) to be needed for proper disclosure or protection of the invention, and (B) to require no substantial amount of additional work by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical sufficient reasons for recommending non-entry include: (A) an additional search is required; (B) more than a cursory review of the record is necessary; (C) the amendment would involve materially added work (e.g., extensive editorial checking). For added claims, dependent claims may be less likely to trigger non-entry but new matter, sufficiency, or undue multiplicity may still arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.111(c) novelty statement requirement applies to 1.312 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 1.312 that add or amend claims must comply with 37 CFR 1.111(c) by pointing out the patentable novelty of any claim sought to be added or amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks accompanying the amendment must fully and clearly state the reasons relied upon to show patentability; see MPEP §§ 713.04 and 713.10 regarding interviews and claim support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after payment of issue fee — petition and fee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after payment of the issue fee must be accompanied by a petition and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i) and a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented; such petitions are decided by the Group Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 13.10 where no petition and/or fee has been filed. Examiner should explain why amendment is needed, why no additional search/examination is required, why claims are patentable, and why they weren't earlier presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 is not a means for continued prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.312 was not intended to provide a way to continue prosecution after an application has been passed for issue; consideration under 1.312 cannot be demanded as a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommendation is against entry, a brief statement such as 'proposed claim not obviously allowable' is sufficient; detailed statements are not necessary for refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copied patent claims received after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment received after notice of allowance includes claims copied or substantially copied from a patent, entry of such copied claims is not a matter of right and is governed by MPEP § 2305.04 and related rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.19 for conditions where copied claims may be refused entry; special fee considerations may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and examiner recommendation procedure for 1.312 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 1.312 are sent by OIPE to Publishing Division, which forwards the proposed amendment, file, and drawings to the examining group; the examiner must promptly consider and indicate 'Enter — 312', 'Do Not Enter' or 'Enter In Part' in red ink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If favorably considered, entry is made and a Response to Rule 312 Communication (PTOL-271) is prepared and signed by the primary examiner; use form paragraphs 7.85 (entered) or 7.87 (not entered) as appropriate. When not entered, the examiner should provide reasons on PTOL-271.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing changes in 37 CFR 1.312 amendments (form paragraph 6.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 1.312 amendment includes proposed drawing changes that are acceptable, include form paragraph 6.48 to give applicant ONE MONTH (or until expiration of Notice of Allowance period, whichever is longer) to file corrected drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when amendment includes a drawing correction proposal; follow drawing correction timing and submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments correcting only formal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that merely correct formal matters in the specification or drawings, or formal matters in a claim without changing scope, or cancel claims may be entered by the primary examiner (notation 'Enter Formal Matters Only').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments do not require SPE prior submission. If disapproved in whole or part, SPE signature is required. PTOL-271 is date stamped and mailed by the examining group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering amendments in part under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the general rule is that an amendment should not be entered in part, when an amendment contains multiple changes some acceptable and some not, the acceptable portions should be entered and the refused portions canceled (in pencil) and noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit PTOL-271 recommending entry of acceptable portion and non-entry of remaining portion with reasons; indicate which claims are entered; applicant may be notified using form paragraph 7.86. Entry-in-part is not recommended unless any full additional fee required accompanies the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment filed after the period for reply expired
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment is filed after the statutory or set period for reply without a petition for extension (37 CFR 1.136(a)), it shall be endorsed on the file wrapper but not formally entered; applicant is immediately notified by telephone and form PTOL-327 that the amendment was not timely filed and application is abandoned unless a petition and fee are timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 711.02 and § 710.02(e) for extension and petition procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stamping, paper numbering and prompt handling of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are stamped with both 'Group Date' (date received in examining group) and 'Office Date' (date received by the Office); the Office Date should be used in communications to applicant. All amendments received in technical support are processed and delivered to the SPE for review and distribution, and mail deliveries should be screened promptly (24 hours) to find replies to final actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After entry, amendment is placed on examiner's desk as 'up for action' and inspected per MPEP § 714.05. If no immediate action required, case awaits regular examination order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — unpatentable/new-search when prosecution closed
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting an unpatentable claim, or a claim requiring a new search or raising a new issue in an application whose prosecution before the primary examiner has been closed (e.g., all claims allowed; all claims finally rejected; some claims allowed and remainder finally rejected) is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 714.12–714.14 for exceptions. A subsequent showing by applicant may lead to entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — substitute specification noncompliant with 37 CFR 1.125
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.125 will ordinarily be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 608.01(q) and 714.20 for substitute specification submission standards and acceptance practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — examiner-suggested claim presented late
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent claim suggested by the examiner and not presented within the time limit set (or extension) is ordinarily denied entry unless entry is authorized by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2305.03 for practice regarding examiner-suggested claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — copied patent claims under certain conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: While copied patent claims are generally admitted even if case under final rejection or on appeal, under certain conditions such claims may be refused entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2307.03 and 714.16(a) for conditions and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — unsigned or improperly signed papers
rubrics_metrics.description: An unsigned or improperly signed amendment, or one signed by a suspended or excluded attorney/agent, is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure signatures comply with applicable rules; if defective, notify applicant and do not enter until corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — filed after statutory period without extension
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed in the PTO after the expiration of the statutory period or set time period for reply, and without appropriate extension, is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.17 and § 711.02 for extension/petition procedures and applicant notification practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — cannot be entered with accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment so worded that it cannot be entered with certain accuracy will ordinarily be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.23 for examples and guidance on insufficiently precise amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — canceling all claims with no substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after the filing date canceling all of the claims and presenting no substitute claims is ordinarily denied entry (nonresponsive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 711.01 for handling and applicant notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — beyond examiner jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment in an application no longer within the examiner's jurisdiction (with certain exceptions for in-issue applications) is ordinarily denied entry except on approval of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.16 regarding practice for applications in issue and supervisory approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — drawing changes alleged to contain new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the drawing held by the examiner to contain new matter are not entered until the new-matter issue is settled; this practice does not apply to specification and claim amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 608.04 and 706.03(o) for new-matter drawing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendatory papers with objectionable remarks (37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendatory paper containing objectionable remarks that, in the examiner's opinion, are within the condemnation of 37 CFR 1.3 will be submitted to the Group Director for return to applicant; if the Group Director finds a violation, the paper will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 714.25 and 1003 for examples and handling procedures; returned paper treatment explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not in permanent ink or on easily erasable paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments not in permanent ink or on so-called easily erasable paper are ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.07 for acceptable submission media and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments exceeding paid claim count without fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for and not accompanied by the full fee for the claims (or authorization to charge a deposit account) is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 607 for fee requirements and charging practices; require full fee with amendment to consider entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment presenting only nonelected invention (nonresponsive)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to the nonelected invention is nonresponsive and should not be entered; applicant should be notified as directed in MPEP §§ 714.03 and 714.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 821.03 for elected/nonelected practice and notification procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent entry of amendments has no legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If technical support staff inadvertently enters an amendment that should not have been entered, such entry has no legal effect; the changes are not legally made and should be noted as 'Not Officially Entered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If retained in the file, give the paper a paper number and list on file wrapper with notation 'Not Entered.' See 37 CFR 1.3 and MPEP § 714.25 for examples of papers to be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making amendments (37 CFR 1.121) — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in nonprovisional applications (except reissue) are made by filing a paper in compliance with § 1.52 directing specified amendments, indicating precise insertion/deletion points and setting forth matter to be inserted/deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insertions must indicate precise point in the specification; deletions must indicate precise point and matter to be deleted. Matter deleted can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting previously deleted matter as a new insertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendment limitations (37 CFR 1.121) — addition of words and rewriting
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be amended by specifying exact matter to be deleted/inserted where changes are limited to deletions and/or addition of no more than five (5) words in any one claim; otherwise a claim must be cancelled or rewritten with underlining for additions and brackets for deletions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rewriting, underlining/bracketing are applied relative to the previous version; parenthetical expressions 'twice amended', 'three times amended', etc., must follow original claim number. A canceled claim can be reinstated only by presenting it as a new claim with a new claim number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendment rules (37 CFR 1.121 & 1.84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to original application drawings are not permitted; any change to the drawings must be by submission of a substitute sheet of drawings for each sheet changed in compliance with § 1.84. Alternatively, a sketch in permanent ink showing proposed changes in red may be filed for approval as a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 1.312 amendments involving drawing corrections, use form paragraph 6.48 to set corrected-drawing filing period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure correction and prohibition on new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended when required by the Office to correct inaccuracies and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings. No amendment may introduce new matter into the disclosure of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure amendments do not add new subject matter; corrections should be limited to securing consistency among claim/spec/drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application amendment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in reissue applications must comply with special requirements: provide entire text of newly added/rewritten paragraphs with markings (or a statement deleting a paragraph), indicate precise point in specification, use underlining/brackets for changes, and follow strict rules for claim amendments including presenting entire text of each amended/added claim with markings, not renumbering patent claims, and setting forth status of all claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each amendment must be accompanied by explanation of support in the disclosure on separate page(s). Drawings amendments to patents follow substitute sheet practice and must be identified as 'amended' or 'new.' No reissue patent shall be granted enlarging scope of original patent claims unless applied for within two years of original grant; no amendment may introduce new matter or be made in an expired patent. All amendments must be relative to the patent as of the reissue filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and use of brackets and underlining in claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'brackets' in 37 CFR 1.121(a) means square brackets [ ]; parentheses () are distinct and may be held not fully responsive. Underlining indicates added matter; brackets indicate deleted matter. If a dependent claim is rewritten in independent form, subject matter from the prior independent claim is considered 'added' and should be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous use of brackets/underlining that makes it unclear whether markings are intended to appear in the patent should be clarified by applicant; see form paragraph guidance for examiner notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment adding more than five words to a claim — noncompliance and cure (form paragraph 6.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim amendment requests the addition of more than five words in any one claim without rewriting per 37 CFR 1.121(a)(2)(ii), the reply is not fully responsive and the amendment will not be entered; applicant is given one month (or 30 days) from mailing to supply a compliant amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Use form paragraph 6.33 to notify applicant and specify the filing date of the noncompliant reply in bracket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear use of brackets/underlining — requirement to clarify (form paragraph 6.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where brackets or underlining are used in such a manner that it is unclear whether the marking is intended to appear in the patent (e.g., ambiguous bracket use), the examiner must notify applicant and require clarification; if underlining/bracketing is intended to appear in the published patent applicant must clearly indicate that intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 6.34 to detail the unclear usage and provide applicant opportunity to clarify. Provide filing date and specific unclear markings in the notice.
